jobs.title: MR-0054: Will of Mary Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough (died 23 December 1915), proved at Llandaff on 3 February 1916, with the registry copy and grant
inputs: why: The 1916 probate calendar (p.301) records a grant of probate, not administration, so a will existed and was proved. Under the probate rules of the time the original will and the registry copy were kept by the probate registry, and they are still held. The will would show how a widow "of Great House Farm" described what she left, whether the farm, its stock or any interest in the land is mentioned, and who she named. Effects were £585 7s 6d (about £66,000 at 2026 prices). It is the nearest family-side document to the February 1916 Bute estate tenancy document, which followed within weeks.
likely holder: HM Courts & Tribunals Service, Probate (copy orderable from the probate index); the family (original papers, not checked)

jobs.title: MR-0056: Loss and fire records of the March 1983 Trust warehouse fire
inputs: why: Full title: loss record and fire report for the March 1983 warehouse fire that destroyed Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust finds, Llandough finds among them. A press report of 18 March 1983 (EV-0068) records a warehouse fire that destroyed the Trust's stored finds; finds from Llandough are reported among the losses. A trust that loses its stored finds reports the loss to its trustees and in its annual report, and the fire brigade that attended completed a fire report. These are the only records that would show which Llandough finds and site records burned, and what survived. Heneb, the Trust's successor, replied on 29 October 2026 that it holds no records on the fire or the finds' custody, so the record now sits with other holders. jobs.title: MR-0058: Glamorgan Archives items catalogued but not yet viewed: 1975 County Treasures survey, East Vale Local Plan, civic society files and 1971 aerial photographs
inputs: why: Seven entries in the Glamorgan Archives catalogue describe records bearing on the house and its setting between 1971 and 1992. The catalogue descriptions have been read; the items themselves have not been seen, so what they show is not checked. CVG/EC/3/1/3/13, ‘Photographs of sites in sector 7 of Penarth survey’ (c1975, one bundle), lists ‘Tymawr Farm, Llandough’ among the sites photographed for the South Glamorgan County Treasures survey, alongside School House, St Dochdwy Church and Llandough House. Our inference, not checked: this is Ty Mawr (Great House Farm), not Llandough Farm, and it may be the survey behind the ‘County Treasure’ description of the house relayed in December 1988. CVG/EC/3/1/3/1 probably holds the matching survey form (not checked). D387 holds the Penarth Town Council provisional list for the County Treasures survey, 1975. D1824/4/5, in the Penarth Civic Society planning papers, holds the East Vale Local Plan of 1987 and its 1991 review, with correspondence; a copy would fill MR-0044, whose catalogue entry is at present a placeholder. D1824/4/1 is a file headed ‘CADW’ (November 1990 to March 1992) and D1824/3/7 is the society’s correspondence of 1988-1992. D978/3/2/24-26 are aerial photographs taken on 6 July 1971 of Llandough Hospital and the area towards the Llandough trading estate; whether the farmhouse is in frame is not checked. Parcel: A (the farmhouse) for the survey photograph, form and list; parcel not identified for the local plan, the civic society files and the aerial photographs (the plan’s proposals map and the photograph frames would identify it).

jobs.title: MR-0059: Ownership of the 0.74 ha Leckwith Road objection site beside the former quarry (open question)
inputs: why: The Inspector’s report on objections to the Vale of Glamorgan Unitary Development Plan (volume 2, section C13.3) records objection 232.4 by the Land Division of the Welsh Development Agency, seeking a housing allocation for ‘an area of land measuring about 0.74ha and located on the northern fringe of Llandough’. The report describes it as ‘a sloping area of pasture land with sporadic tree cover’ that ‘abuts Leckwith Road’, with its north-eastern boundary ‘formed by the upper lip of a former quarry/brickworks site now occupied by the Llandough trading estate’, and adds that ‘a previous Inspector also reached a similar conclusion when dismissing an appeal on this site in 1992’. Who owned the site, and whether it was ever part of Great House Farm, is not shown: an objector is not necessarily the owner. Open question: who held the title when the 1992 appeal and the plan objection were made, and whether the land appears in any earlier conveyance of the farm. Parcel not identified: the plan’s objection-site map, the 1992 appeal decision or the registered title plan would identify it.

inputs: why: The replica plans for the house are built from the 1974 measured ground plan (NA/GL/89/208) and the 1974 record card, which give the outline and the room sizes.
